method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: PRINTED NAME: both plates letter this corridor 'AVE. B OR STRAND' down the roadway I measured, and print its width 80' in it (sheet 17 casings native 2028.5/2269.0, sheet 21 casings 2039.5/2281.5, both ~240 native px = 79 ft at this scan's 3.04 px/ft). HUNDRED-BLOCK BREAK ON THE SEAM STREET ITSELF (9th St, which is sheet 17's south edge and sheet 21's north edge, so both plates letter the same frontage): on sheet 17 the cross-street run west of the line is 101 103 105 107 109 111 | 113 115 117 119 121 123 (and 102-124 on the 8th St face), and the first run east of it is 201 203 205 207 / 202 204 206 208; on sheet 21 the run west of the line is 101 103 105 107 109 111 | 113 115 117 119 121 123 with 102-122 opposite, and the first run east is again 201 203 205 207 / 202 204 206 208. The same 100|200 transition on the same street - this is the Strand & 9th intersection read off both plates. The corridor's own frontage numbers confirm which streets: sheet 17 carries 801-827 / 802-828 on it (8th-9th block), sheet 21 carries 901-927 / 902-928 (9th-10th) and 1001-1021 / 1002-1022 (10th-11th). ONE AVENUE WEST is AVE. A OR WATER (lettered in its roadway on both plates, east casing native 1232.5 on sheet 17 and 1246.5 on sheet 21, with the wharf-front R.R. curving along it); it bounds the 100 block on the WEST, not the east, so it cannot carry the 100|200 break. ONE AVENUE EAST is AVE. C OR MECHANIC (sheet 17 cand3 letters it, with the whole 200 block - 201-223 / 202-224, blocks 607 and 608 - lying between Strand and Mechanic; casings 3057.0/3305.5 on sheet 17, 3075.0/3309.5 on sheet 21); it carries the 200|300 break. Neither alternative shows 100|200, so neither can be this line. NOTE ON THE TASK KEYMAP: task.json describes sheet 17 as an isolated SW outlot plate at 50th-52nd Sts with no avenues printed. The actual sheet-17 raster does not show that: it shows Seawall Blvd, 8TH ST and 9TH ST, John Sealy Hospital (blocks 667/668) and University Hall, letters AVE. A OR WATER, AVE. B OR STRAND and AVE. C OR MECHANIC, prints '21' in its bottom margin and '18' in its east margin - i.e. exactly the plate directly above sheet 21, whose own crops print '17' in their top margin. I went with the printed evidence; the keymap note for 17 appears to be attached to the wrong unit. NOTE ON THE PROPOSED CANDIDATES (none is an avenue): the detector returned the identical triple 1763 / 748 / 2778 on BOTH sheets. On each plate 1763 lands inside the block interior between street numbers 115 and 117, with the 100-block run continuing unbroken across it and no avenue name; 748 and 2778 likewise fall inside block interiors near the 20-ft mid-block alleys (drawn dashed and labelled 8" W. PIPE / 6" W. PIPE, printed 20'). Reporting any of them would shear the map. CORROBORATION: the sheet-to-sheet offset b-a from Strand is +12.8 px; the same offset read from Ave A's east casing is +14.0 and from Mechanic's centre +11.0, so the control is consistent to ~1.5 px. Independent check against an existing control: pair_21_27_x reads sheet 21's Strand as 2156.7 at its SOUTH (12th St) seam; my full-height profile of the same corridor on u21 gives 2157.2-2157.6 in that row band, agreeing to under a pixel.
measurement_note: Native x = raster x of work/sheets/1912w/u<unit>.jpg (3327x3898), origin top-left. Value is the midpoint of the two block-face casing lines bounding the 80-ft Strand roadway, measured in the block row ADJACENT TO THE 9th St SEAM (sheet 17 y 2700-3500, centres 2149.2 -> 2147.8 with a slight southward drift, extrapolated to the seam at y~3600: 2147.7; sheet 21 y 0-1100, centres 2160.5-2160.7, at the seam y~200: 2160.5). Both plates carry a small drafted skew (sheet 17 Strand drifts 2149.6 at y2100 to 2147.8 at y3500; sheet 21 drifts 2160.6 at the top to 2157.4 at the bottom), so the near-seam reading is the one to use. Ruler-read values off the supplied crops (sheet_17_cand1, sheet_21_cand1) reproduce these to 0.4 px.
